analysis.title: Midday Market Intelligence: post-election
key_insights: US stocks are broadly higher on Wednesday 4 Nov 2026 after the US Midterm Elections. GS reads the move as relief that the event is over, with nearly every S&P 500 sector higher. Only Energy and Industrials lag, and Consumer Discretionary, Communication Services and Staples lead.

Alec Phillips believes the larger-than-expected Democratic majorities in the House and Senate could give Democrats slightly more leverage in negotiations with the White House. They would also dilute the influence of small factions within the Democratic caucus.
Carly Davenport flags a potential risk to Texas-exposed power stocks including NRG and VST from early state election results.

Rates are lower on the day, which helps longer-duration assets including Mega Cap Tech. Brent is down 9.5% to $93.77/bbl, the first time at that level in two months. GS links the drop to optimism about a possible end to the Iran War. Lower oil and lower rates are also lifting consumer stocks.

Block (XYZ) is the best performing S&P 500 stock after a solid 3Q26 beat, driven by the Cash app business and its payment processing platform for businesses. Will Nance's note cites a beat and raise with preliminary 2027 guidance.

FIS is the worst performing S&P 500 stock after better-than-expected but lower quality 3Q26 results. Higher non-recurring revenue was offset by lower recurring banking revenue growth, which led to lower forward guidance. The company also announced a CFO transition.

BKNG reported solid results citing stable travel demand, share gains and AI use. BKNG and EXPE (reporting tonight) are among the better performers, possibly helped by hope for an Iran War resolution and lower oil prices.
AMD reported very strong Datacenter growth across server CPUs and GPUs. GS sees clear visibility to over 80% company-level revenue growth in 2027 despite PC market headwinds, and rates the stock Buy.

The ISM non-manufacturing survey declined slightly, roughly in line with consensus. Employment rose while new orders and business activity fell. Together with ISM Manufacturing, the surveys point to healthy activity but no surge to a far-above-trend pace. Price components eased in October but stay above pre-Iran-war levels.
Chart of the Day: GS raised its global data center capacity forecast to 273 GW of live capacity by 2030, up from about 103 GW in 2025, a 21% 2025-2030 CAGR.
Watch weekly jobless claims on Thursday. Many earnings reports follow today after the close, including QCOM, APP, COST, EXPE and COHR, and Thursday before the open, including COP, CMI, APD and ZTS.

geopolitical: US Midterm Elections: Democrats won a House and Senate majority with gains well above expectations. Markets read the result as relief that the event is over.
Iran War: markets show increased optimism about a potential end to the war, reflected in Brent falling 9.5% to $93.77/bbl. Oil prices linked to the war have been a headwind to travel demand.
